problem_summary.summary: Rotate an n x n image 90 degrees clockwise by modifying its matrix in place without allocating another matrix.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: an n x n integer matrix. Rotate it in place; the method returns nothing.

brute_force.explanation: Allocate a second n x n matrix and move every source value at (row, col) to (col, n - 1 - row). Copy the rotated values back into the input.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A clockwise quarter-turn maps each source coordinate (row, col) to destination (col, n - 1 - row), so every value lands in its required rotated position.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) — each cell is moved once and the result is copied back once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n^2) auxiliary for the second matrix.

optimized.explanation: Transpose the matrix by swapping entries above the main diagonal with their mirrored entries below it, then reverse each row. The composition is a clockwise 90-degree rotation.
optimized.correctness_idea: Transposition maps (row, col) to (col, row); reversing each row then maps that position to (col, n - 1 - row), the required clockwise destination. Each pair is swapped once, so the operation stays in place.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n^2) — transposition and row reversal each touch O(n^2) positions overall.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — the matrix is transformed using swaps and scalar variables.

steps.event: Transpose by swapping matrix[0][1] and matrix[1][0].
steps.condition: col > row, so this off-diagonal pair is processed once.

steps.event: Continue transposition: swap [0,2], then [1,2] with their mirrored cells.
steps.condition: Each column index is greater than its row index.

steps.event: Reverse row 0 by swapping its endpoints.
Reverse row 1 by swapping its endpoints.
Reverse row 2 by swapping its endpoints.

edge_cases.handling: There are no off-diagonal or row-endpoint swaps; the matrix is unchanged.
The center cell and each row's middle cell remain in place, as required by rotation.
Values are moved by position only; their signs do not affect the transformation.
